newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Zwack says black market hit 1996 profits.
newsitem.headline: Zwack says black market hit 1996 profits.

text.p: Hungarian spirits maker Zwack said on Friday a smaller legal domestic alcoholic drinks market and a failure to curb black market sales had contributed to a drop in 1996 operating profit.

"The legal drinks market continued to shrink as in previous years," Zwack said in its preliminary 1996 earnings report. "Measures announced by the government to push back the black market did not show any result last year."
The company said a bumper fruit crop in the summer had led to an increase in home-made liquor and led to a dramatic fall in fourth quarter sales.

The company, most famous for its flagship drink Unicum, reported its IAS consolidated operating profit falling to 952 million forints from 1.02 billion in 1995 despite an increase in net sales to 8.29 billion forints from 6.94 billion in 1995.
